subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The first stage of treating fresh water to make it potable is usually:
questions.explain: Water is first filtered through filter beds to remove insoluble solids before sterilisation.

questions.q: Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace by reduction with which substance?
questions.explain: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon reduces iron oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels described as finite resources?
options: They form much faster than we use them
They are being used up faster than they form
questions.explain: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so they are finite and being used up faster than they are replaced.

questions.q: Bronze is an alloy mainly of copper and which other element?
questions.explain: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

questions.q: Which human activity increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, adding to atmospheric levels.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.

questions.q: How does galvanising protect iron from rusting?
options: By adding carbon to the iron
By coating it with a layer of zinc
questions.explain: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which acts as both a barrier and sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Incomplete combustion of fuels can produce which toxic gas?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas produced by incomplete combustion when oxygen is limited.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, oxidation is best described as:
questions.explain: Using OILRIG, Oxidation Is Loss of electrons.

questions.q: What is meant by the carbon footprint of a product?
options: The amount of carbon it contains only
The total greenhouse gases emitted over its life cycle
questions.explain: A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases emitted over the full life cycle of a product or service.

questions.q: In treating potable water from fresh sources, sterilisation is used to:
questions.explain: Sterilisation, for example with chlorine, kills harmful microbes in drinking water.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
Aluminium does not form an ore
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide and electrolysis must be used.
